subject: Implementation de-risking & staged migration MAP - Lighthouse Health
thread_text:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@lighthousehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation de-risking & staged migration MAP - Lighthouse Health

Sara —

Congratulations again on signing SOW RH-0047. Per our discussion last week, attached is the first draft of a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds a staged post-signature implementation: a short pilot/canary, a phased migration window, and a two-week training & enablement cadence for your ops and developer teams. The goal is to reduce cutover risk and provide measurable checkpoints we can use to gate the go/no-go decisions.

Key highlights in this draft:
- Week 1: Canary pilot (2 small services) with 4-hour monitoring windows and rollback criteria documented.
- Weeks 2–4: Phase 1 migration (non-critical traffic, read-only paths) with KV cache warm-up and latency SLO validation.
- Weeks 5–8: Full migration with traffic shift up to 80% and a hypercare rotation for our engineers.
- Training: Two instructor-led sessions (0.5 day each) and an on-demand lab for your platform team.
- Success gates: latency < 150ms p95, error rate < 0.5%, and no P1 incidents during the 72h post-shift window.

I attached Lighthouse_MAP_v1.2.xlsx with a lane-by-lane timeline and the Canary_Runbook.pdf that defines the monitoring/rollback play. Please review and flag any dates that conflict with your blackout windows.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Your IT team confirms blackout windows and network checklist by Wed Aug 26
2) We finalize canary targets and runbook by Fri Aug 28
3) Kickoff canary Mon Aug 31 (can be shifted if needed)

If you prefer, we can run a short alignment call Wednesday — Marissa and Priyom will drive orchestration and migration automation respectively.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122

Subject: Re: Implementation de-risking & staged migration MAP - Lighthouse Health

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the thorough draft. A few quick questions from our side:

1) For the canary, can we define the services by API path rather than "small services"? We want to limit exposure to patient-facing endpoints.
2) We have a planned maintenance window Sep 2–3 that affects our auth layer — can we avoid scheduling critical migration steps during that timeframe?
3) Our security team will need the network matrix and the KMS/HSM details for the private deployment path — can your team provide a short write-up and the SOC2 evidence pointer?

Tom, looping you for the blackout window confirmation.

Sara Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Lighthouse Health
sara@lighthousehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-9900

Sara — thanks for the quick review and the blackout heads-up. Answering your bullets: 

1) Canary targets: absolutely — we'll map explicit API paths and provide a make/model list of the two endpoints we'll route (we suggest /api/v1/clinical/search and /api/v1/notes/read as low-risk read-heavy candidates). If LH prefers patient-facing endpoints excluded, we'll flag only internal tooling or anonymized read flows.

2) Maintenance window: we will move any critical auth-dependent cutover steps to after Sep 3. I'll mark Sep 2–3 as blackout in the MAP and shift the Phase 2 migration window accordingly.

3) Security evidence: attaching network_matrix.xlsx here and linking to our SOC2 report in the MAP folder. Priyom — can you add a one-page HSM/KMS summary for Sara's team and drop it in the Drive link?

I also included two acceptance criteria tweaks to keep the canary conservative: limit canary duration to 72h and a manual hold point for configuration changes.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Sara / team —

I'll take the HSM/KMS one-pager and the network FAQ. Quick notes from an implementation perspective:
- We'll propose an initial canary traffic cap of 1% with header-based routing so you can scope by API path.
- Canary telemetry will be pushed to your Datadog account (read-only API key) and our dashboard; we will also provide an ephemeral rollback flag that your team can toggle.
- For KV cache warm-up we recommend a synthetic prefix-warm job running 12–24h before Phase 1 traffic shift.

Deliverables I'll drop in the Drive folder by EOD Aug 26: HSM-KMS-summary.md, canary-config.yaml, and a brief runbook excerpt.

—Priyom
